The Homeland Security Improvement Act (H.R. 1678) directly addresses accountability gaps by mandating independent oversight commissions and standardized complaint processes for detention facilities. Section 3 establishes an Ombudsman to investigate abuses, while Section 6 requires body-camera usage and data tracking on enforcement actions.

The bill allocates $55 million annually for facility upgrades and medical staffing—yet DHS continues funneling funds into outdated detention models instead of modernized alternatives. Overcrowding at Krome isn’t accidental; it’s the result of a bloated bureaucracy prioritizing detention quotas over humane solutions.

Real reform requires dismantling the profit-driven detention industrial complex, not performative oversight theatrics.
